raw_case_text:
A 35-year-old lady was admitted due to fever (39 C), abdominal pain, diarrhea and a non-productive cough for 3 days. She reported a history of asthma, atopic dermatitis, nephrolithiasis and smoking (30 pack/year). Her abdominal problems started 1 year ago when she underwent multiple urgent or semi-elective operations: appendectomy with subsequent gallbladder removal, followed by diagnostic laparotomy (6 months ago) with biopsies from a thickened jejunum to identify evidence of eosinophilic enteritis (muscular and serosal layers). She received treatment with steroids that was discontinued 2 months prior to admission.
On admission she presented with tachypnea, tachycardia, fever, and fine crackles in the right upper pulmonary field. Abdominal examination identified diffuse rebound tenderness and ascites. Chest-radiograph showed a consolidation in the right upper pulmonary field (Fig. 1), air blood gases (ABGs) revealed hypocapnea, and blood tests showed leukocytosis (without eosinophilia), high CRP and D-dimers, low albumin and marginally low sodium (Table 1). She received oxygen (28%), i.v. clarithromycin and cefuroxime, fluids, ranitidine, analgesics, and low-molecular-weight heparin subcutaneously.
Because of the severe clinical picture, impaired ABGs and the lung infiltrate, she underwent a ventilation/perfusion scan indicating a low probability for PE. On day 2 she had an unenhanced (due to strong history of allergy and no time for desensitization) spiral abdominal CT (Fig. 2), which showed a large amount of free fluid collection and thickening of several small bowel loops, without evidence of perforation. She did not consent to abdominal paracentesis. Viral and microbiology serological tests, as well as blood, urine and stool cultures were screened. Sputum induction gave suboptimal material for cultures.
The patient gradually improved. An upper GI endoscopy was unremarkable and biopsies showed mild gastritis. As diarrhea gradually improved and ceased, and given that the patient had twice had a lower GI endoscopy over the previous months, with unremarkable findings, a third colonoscopy was postponed. PPD was negative. She underwent a spiral chest-CT negative for PE, while the lung lesion resolved. Her immunological tests showed very high IgE, with IgA, IgM, IgG, RF, ANA, ANCA within normal values. Hepatotropic viruses, adenovirus, CMV, HIV, EBV, Coxiella burnetii, Yersinia enterocolitica, and Entamoeba histolytica were negative. Stool for parasites and stool-urine-blood cultures were also negative. On admission the patient had a titer for Legionella sp. IgG 1/64 in serum which, when repeated at week 4 from the onset of illness, diagnostically rose to titer 1/128. Urinary test for Legionella was not performed and PCR for Legionella was unavailable from our lab at that time. The final diagnosis for this patient was Legionella pneumophila pneumonia - eosinophilic gastroenteritis.
Abbreviations: CT, computed tomography; CMV, cytomegalovirus; HIV, Human Immunodeficiency Virus; EBV, Epstein Barr Virus
She completed 14 days of antibiotic treatment and had for her EG prednisolone 40 mg slowly tapered, ranitidine 300 mg, ketotifen, and calcium and vitamin-D supplementation. The patient had a straightforward recovery, and she subsequently underwent an MRI-enteroclysis to further study the affected small bowel (Fig. 3). Three years after the episode she remains asymptomatic without relapses.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old female with biopsy-proven eosinophilic enteritis presented with a 3-day history of high fever (39 C), abdominal pain, diarrhea, and non-productive cough.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed acute fever (39 C), abdominal pain, diarrhea, and dry cough 3 days prior to admission. Her chronic abdominal symptoms had begun 1 year earlier, leading to urgent appendectomy, cholecystectomy, and a diagnostic laparotomy 6 months prior that showed muscular and serosal eosinophilic enteritis of the jejunum; she had been treated with oral corticosteroids, which were discontinued 2 months before the current admission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Biopsy-proven muscular/serosal jejunal eosinophilic enteritis (diagnosed 6 months ago, off steroids for 2 months), asthma, atopic dermatitis, nephrolithiasis, prior appendectomy and cholecystectomy, and two unremarkable lower GI endoscopies in the preceding months. Social history: 30 pack-year smoking history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever (39 C), abdominal pain, diarrhea, and non-productive cough.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vitals/general: febrile (39 C), tachypneic, and tachycardic. Chest auscultation: fine crackles in the right upper pulmonary field. Abdominal examination: diffuse rebound tenderness and clinical ascites.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood tests: leukocytosis without eosinophilia, elevated CRP, elevated D-dimers, hypoalbuminemia, and mildly low serum sodium. Arterial blood gases (ABGs) showed hypocapnia. Chest radiograph demonstrated a right upper lobe pulmonary consolidation. Tuberculin skin test (PPD) was negative. Blood, urine, and stool cultures and stool ova/parasite examinations were negative; sputum induction yielded suboptimal material. Serologies for Entamoeba histolytica, hepatotropic viruses, adenovirus, CMV, HIV, EBV, Coxiella burnetii, and Yersinia enterocolitica were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) lung scan showed low probability for pulmonary embolism, and subsequent spiral chest CT was negative for PE and showed resolution of the lung infiltrate. Day-2 unenhanced spiral abdominal CT (unenhanced due to severe allergy history) revealed large-volume free peritoneal fluid (ascites) and thickening of multiple small bowel loops without perforation (patient declined paracentesis). Upper GI endoscopy was unremarkable with biopsies showing mild gastritis. Immunological workup showed markedly elevated total IgE with normal IgA, IgM, IgG, RF, ANA, and ANCA. Follow-up MRI-enteroclysis was performed to evaluate the small bowel.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Paired serum Legionella sp. IgG titers demonstrated a diagnostic rise from 1:64 on admission to 1:128 at week 4 from symptom onset (while Entamoeba histolytica serology, stool parasites, and bacterial/viral cultures were negative), confirming Legionella pneumophila pneumonia concomitant with a flare of eosinophilic gastroenteritis (with amoebiasis and pulmonary embolism ruled out). She was treated with oxygen (28%), 14 days of intravenous clarithromycin and cefuroxime, IV fluids, ranitidine (300 mg), subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin, and a slow taper of oral prednisolone (starting at 40 mg) plus ketotifen, calcium, and vitamin D supplementation. She recovered completely and remained relapse-free at 3-year follow-up.
